title: US Treasury demand is holding, but the buyer base is shifting
gist: Overall US Treasury demand is holding up, but the buyer base is rotating away from weakening foreign buyers toward more price-sensitive domestic investment funds and leveraged investors, while the Treasury responds by tilting issuance shorter-term.

insights.claim: Foreign demand for US Treasuries has weakened, forcing increased reliance on domestic investment funds and leveraged investors to absorb issuance.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: A buyer base tilting toward price-sensitive domestic funds and leveraged accounts can mean more volatile, less sticky demand at auctions, raising the risk of yield spikes if these buyers pull back.
insights.quote: Recent data indicates that foreign demand for Treasuries has weakened, leading to increased reliance on domestic investment funds and leveraged investors.
insights.locator: Recent data indicates that foreign demand

insights.claim: The overall shift in Treasury demand is toward more price-sensitive buyers, a structural change in market dynamics rather than a temporary blip.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Price-sensitive buyers require higher yields to absorb the same supply, implying a structurally higher term premium and more auction-driven yield volatility going forward.
insights.quote: Treasury demand is evolving, with a notable shift towards more price-sensitive buyers amid changing market dynamics.
insights.locator: Treasury demand is evolving, with a notable shift

insights.claim: Treasury yields are expected to stay elevated in the near term but decline gradually as inflation pressures ease.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Investors should not expect near-term relief in Treasury yields; the disinflation-driven decline is a gradual, multi-quarter process rather than an imminent drop.
insights.locator: While Treasury yields are expected to remain elevated

insights.claim: The Federal Reserve is likely to stay hawkish through 2026 because of persistent inflation, but easing services inflation and a cooling labour market should prevent further rate hikes.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: A 'hawkish but done hiking' Fed stance through 2026 argues against pricing in additional tightening, while also delaying rate-cut expectations that would otherwise pull yields lower.
insights.quote: The Federal Reserve is likely to maintain a hawkish stance through 2026 due to persistent inflation, but easing services inflation and a cooling labour market may prevent further rate hikes.
insights.locator: The Federal Reserve is likely to maintain a hawkish stance

themes.theme: Long-end yield drivers and issuance strategy

insights.claim: Long-end Treasury yields are projected to fall only slowly, held up by heavy Treasury supply, geopolitical uncertainty, and record corporate borrowing linked to AI investment.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: AI-driven corporate debt issuance is now cited as a competing claim on capital that keeps long-end Treasury yields sticky, a channel worth tracking alongside fiscal supply when positioning duration.
insights.quote: Long-end yields are projected to fall slowly, influenced by heavy Treasury supply and geopolitical uncertainties, alongside record corporate borrowing linked to AI investments.
insights.locator: Long-end yields are projected to fall slowly

insights.claim: The US Treasury plans to adjust its issuance strategy by focusing more on shorter-term securities to manage rising borrowing needs.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: A tilt toward bill/short-tenor issuance reduces near-term reliance on price-sensitive long-end buyers but raises rollover risk and keeps the Treasury more exposed to future rate moves.
insights.quote: The Treasury plans to adjust its issuance strategy, focusing more on shorter-term securities to manage rising borrowing needs effectively.
insights.locator: The Treasury plans to adjust its issuance strategy
